title: Operations Control Policy: Rebooking After Irregular Operations
content:
**Operations Control policy — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** Operations control records every irregular operation affecting a ticketed segment as a disruption record — a delay, a cancellation, a missed connection caused by an inbound Crestline delay, a schedule change, a denied boarding, an involuntary downgrade or a delayed bag — each with its cause.

## Cause of a disruption

| Cause recorded | Examples in the policy |
|---|---|
| Controllable | Crew, maintenance, IT, catering, fueling or other causes within Crestline's control |
| Uncontrollable | Weather, air traffic control, airport authority, security or medical diversions |

The cause on the disruption record is authoritative, and a customer's account of the cause never replaces it.

## Rebooking right

When a flight is cancelled, a connection is missed, the passenger is denied boarding or a schedule change is significant, the passenger is rebooked free of change fee and fare difference on the next Crestline flight with a seat in the same cabin to the same destination, on every fare brand including Crestline Basic Economy.

- A reaccommodation is recorded only against an existing disruption record on the same ticket whose disruption type is cancellation, missed connection, denied boarding or schedule change.
- Reaccommodation is available only while the ticket is ticketed or partially flown.
- Rebooking on a partner carrier is offered only when the earliest Crestline alternative arrives at least the fare brand's partner rebooking threshold in hours after the original scheduled arrival.
- The rebooked flight replaces the disrupted segment, and the ticket's next departure is updated to it.

## Declining, and delays below the threshold

A customer may decline the rebooking and take an involuntary refund under the refund rule instead; the two are mutually exclusive for the same disruption. A delay below the significant schedule-change thresholds on a flight that still operates gives no rebooking right; the customer may buy a same-day change under that rule.

| Disruption type on the record (hypothetical) | Reaccommodation may be recorded against it |
|---|---|
| Cancellation | Yes |
| Missed connection | Yes |
| Denied boarding | Yes |
| Schedule change | Yes |
| Delay, involuntary downgrade, delayed bag | No |
